title: Sisi Inaugurates EGP 800 Billion New Delta Agricultural Megaproject
detail: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi formally inaugurated the New Delta project on the Sheikh Zayed Axis in Giza — one of the largest agricultural infrastructure investments in Egypt's modern history. The project converts approximately 2.2 million feddans (~920,000 hectares) of Western Desert land into productive farmland, increasing Egypt's total cultivated area by over 20%. At an estimated cost of EGP 800 billion (~USD 15 billion), it is projected to create around 2 million jobs and significantly reduce Egypt's food import dependence. Prime Minister Madbouly subsequently confirmed that the project expands cultivated land by more than 20%, marking the most ambitious Egyptian desert reclamation effort since the Toshka scheme of the 1990s.

media.caption: President El-Sisi inaugurates the New Delta agricultural megaproject at EGP 800 billion

title: IMF Seventh Review Mission Arrives in Cairo; ~$1.7 Billion Disbursement Expected in June
detail: An IMF delegation arrived in Cairo on May 17 to begin the seventh review of Egypt's $8 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) approved in March 2024. A successful review is expected to unlock approximately $1.6–1.7 billion in new disbursements at a June 2026 board meeting, bringing total EFF drawdowns to roughly $7.5 billion. The mission focused heavily on privatization pipeline progress — a key program benchmark — alongside exchange rate flexibility and fiscal consolidation targets. The seventh review follows the February 2026 combined 5th/6th review that disbursed $2.27 billion. The IMF delegation concluded its Cairo visit by May 24 ahead of the scheduled board meeting.

media.caption: IMF seventh review mission arrives in Cairo to assess Egypt's EFF program progress
